title: Apple Faces Korean Regulator Review Over iPhone 16 AI Advertising
summary: Apple is facing a formal probe in South Korea over allegations that its iPhone 16 advertising misled consumers about the availability of Apple Intelligence features. Investigators at the country's Fair Trade Commission (FTC) have referred Apple and Apple Korea for review , alleging that several Apple Intelligence features were not delivered as advertised, including Genmoji, Image Playground, and Siri's ability to understand personal context and onscreen awareness. The allegations focus on whether Apple adequately explained which features were available and when others would arrive. For example, the FTC's report notes that Siri's personal-context capabilities were advertised for Korean availability in early April 2025 but did not arrive until October 2026, approximately 18 months later. Apple provided MacRumors with the following statement: "At Apple, we deeply value the relationship with our customers in Korea and have always focused on delivering the best products and services in the world. Since we added Korean language support for Apple Intelligence last year, users have benefited from dozens of powerful features that are integrated across Apple's platforms. And we have continued to build on that commitment with the recent launch of Korean language support for Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri that's more capable, conversational, and personal. We have cooperated with the KFTC's investigation and disagree with the conclusions in the Examiner's Report. We look forward to presenting a fulsome defense before the Commission." The Commission has yet to issue a final ruling or impose a penalty. The case follows similar complaints about Apple Intelligence advertising in the United States and other major Apple markets. In April 2025, Apple removed its "available now" marketing claim on its Apple Intelligence page, following a National Advertising Division inquiry. The advertising watchdog found that the wording implied that all listed features were available, and that a footnote explaining the phased rollout was insufficiently clear. Apple disagreed with the findings but ultimately complied with the recommendation. Apple also agreed to a $250 million settlement in May 2026 over a U.S. class-action lawsuit alleging it misled buyers about the availability of Apple Intelligence and Siri features when the iPhone 16 was released in September 2024. title: Apple Still Working on Giant Foldable iPad That Could Cost $5,000
summary: Apple is still developing a large foldable iPad despite ongoing technical challenges and uncertainty about whether it will ever launch, according to Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman . Speaking on the latest episode of the "Power On" podcast , Gurman revived discussion about the device, known internally as "Project J312." He described it as a foldable iPad with a display measuring around 19 to 20 inches, saying it would resemble a "gigantic iPhone Duo with no display on the outside." The device could cost between $3,000 and $5,000. Apple apparently originally wanted to announce the device by 2027, before pushing that target to 2028. The timeframe has since slipped to around 2029, although Gurman cautioned that it remains uncertain whether the product will ever reach the market. Gurman cited cost and display manufacturing yield issues among the obstacles facing development, along with concerns that the ‌iPad‌ could be cumbersome. Apple has also yet to determine which operating system it would run, with macOS, iPadOS, and an entirely new platform all remaining possibilities. Gurman described the unresolved software direction as another complication, but expressed excitement about the device's potential. The comments follow a report from research firm Omdia in September, which claimed that Apple had canceled plans for a foldable MacBook measuring between 16.1 and 18 inches when unfolded. Earlier reports had described that device as a large-screened foldable ‌iPad‌, although it remains unclear whether Omdia was referring to the same project Gurman discussed. Gurman discussed the foldable ‌iPad‌ in April, describing it as a priority for John Ternus while warning that it could remain an unreleased experiment. The potential 2029 timeframe was already part of Gurman's report from October 2025 , when weight and display technology issues were said to threaten Apple's earlier 2028 target. title: iPhone 20 Pro Could Feature Ceramic in Limited-Edition Model
summary: Apple could offer a limited-edition iPhone 20 Pro model that incorporates ceramic, according to the Chinese leaker known as Fixed Focus Digital. In a post on Weibo , the leaker claimed to have gotten their hands on ceramic components for the 20th-anniversary iPhone, which is expected to launch next year. In a follow-up comment, the leaker claimed that the project would enter mass production if it passes engineering validation testing (EVT), and even joked that its scarcity could make it appreciate in value. The leaker doesn't say what kind of ceramic components they have in their possession, leaving it unclear whether Apple is considering a ceramic rear panel, a larger section of the enclosure, or a smaller exterior part. The company also previously sold ceramic Apple Watch Edition models, including a white ceramic version of the Series 5. Interestingly, the ‌iPhone Air‌ features Ceramic Shield 2 on the front and Ceramic Shield on the back, and Fixed Focus Digital has previously said next year's iPhone 20 Pro models will use the same glass design , but with more pronounced curves along all four sides of a titanium frame. Ceramic Shield incorporates tiny ceramic crystals within a glass matrix, which preserves transparency while improving durability. However, the wording of the leaker's latest post suggests that ceramic could be applied in a more visually prominent way. Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone models are expected to launch in the fall of 2027 with a radical glass-centric redesign featuring a quad-curved display . Leakers have variously referred to the device as the "iPhone 20 Pro," but Apple's naming plans remain unclear. The company could well skip the iPhone 19 name to emphasize the anniversary, similar to when it introduced the iPhone X in 2017. title: iPhones Dominate China's Weak Singles' Day Smartphone Sales
summary: Apple held the top spot in China's smartphone market during the country's Singles' Day shopping festival, despite an 8% year-over-year sales decline, according to Counterpoint Research . title: Kodak Launches Unique AirTag Rival With E-Ink Display
summary: Kodak licensee Reto this week introduced the SlideTag, a $34.99 Find My-compatible item tracker with a color E Ink screen for displaying personal photos. The SlideTag's design draws on Kodak's Kodachrome slide mounts, placing a square display inside a retro frame with an attachment point for a keyring. Its 1.54-inch screen has a resolution of 240 × 240 pixels and uses six ink colors to reproduce images. As it is an E Ink panel, it retains a static image without needing continuous power to display it. Users can manage photos through the Kodak Memory Link app for iOS and Android, separately from the accessory's tracking features. They can transfer up to 12 images over Bluetooth and arrange them into slideshows, or use the screen to display information such as contact details, a QR code, or a to-do list. Once paired with Apple's Find My app, the SlideTag can be located through the ‌Find My‌ network. There is also support for Google's Find Hub. A built-in buzzer provides an audible way to find nearby belongings. The device uses a replaceable CR2032 battery and has an IP54 rating for dust and splash resistance. Its plastic enclosure measures 39.3 × 46 × 7.58mm and weighs 16.6 grams, making it wider and taller than the current AirTag , but slightly thinner. Apple's tracker measures 31.9mm in diameter and 8mm thick, and weighs 11.8 grams. The ‌AirTag‌ retains some advantages, including Ultra Wideband technology for Precision Finding, which provides distance and directional guidance to nearby items on compatible devices. The ‌AirTag‌ also has a higher IP67 rating, providing protection against immersion in water up to one meter deep for up to 30 minutes. Reto, which also makes the Kodak-branded Charmera keychain camera, is selling the SlideTag as a collectible. Buyers receive a randomly selected design in sealed packaging, rather than choosing a particular finish. There are eight standard designs and a secret edition that has a one-in-64 chance of appearing. With its combination of a customizable photo display and ‌Find My‌ support, the SlideTag is one of the more unusual item trackers on the market and is available to order from Reto's online store for $34.99.
